Recommendations: 1) National Incident Commander — provisionally approve phased sustainment: retain two forward mobile clinics (one Central, one Northeast) and place the third on national standby for redeployment or demobilization within 24h if both shelter loads and 911 metrics remain stable (decision window 12h); 2) Public Health Operations Desk — within 6h implement staff rotations and a phased demobilization plan with mental‑health support, maintaining surge capacity for 72h unless triggers breach; 3) Joint Transport Ops & Infrastructure & Logistics — within 4h prioritize fuel/top‑up for inbound convoy and returning assets, restrict nonessential convoys, and coordinate air/river resupply contingencies where road fuel limits constrain movement; 4) Infrastructure & Telecom Desk — within 8h resupply the forward telecom team’s spare parts and then rebalance teams to eliminate critical rural 911 gaps while maintaining Northeast coverage. 

Rationale and Assumptions: Provisional allocations aim to sustain life‑safety coverage while avoiding resource depletion, assuming current shelter stability, ~2–3h convoy ETA, continued airlift utilization, and constrained fuel/spare inventories; all tasking should be revised immediately if shelter occupancy, 911 call volumes, or asset readiness indicators worsen (preliminary/unconfirmed data).
